html:
The Emberá are an Indigenous people of eastern Panama and western Colombia, living along the rivers of the Darién and Chocó rainforests. Their languages are Chocoan, shared with the Wounaan.

They live in houses raised on stilts along the rivers, travel by dugout canoe, and farm plantains and maize while hunting and fishing. They paint their bodies with black jagua dye for ceremonies and weave fine baskets. Spanish attempts to subdue the Chocó in the 1600s met strong resistance, and the region's gold drew miners and enslaved Africans. Many Emberá moved north into the Darién of Panama in the 1700s and 1900s. Their neighbours include the Guna and their own branch the Emberá Chamí.
